quote.text: Tyranitar at 14 is exceptional value, filling three needs at once: Sand Stream weather setter, premier physical attacker (134 base Attack), and a bulky Rock/Dark defensive backbone that gets a SpD boost in its own sand.
Excadrill completes the sand core with Tyranitar's Sand Stream, giving me a fast Ground/Steel sweeper under Sand Rush that threatens the Fire, Steel, and Electric types across opponent rosters.
Straight 1-for-1 swap: I get Altaria for its Ground immunity and Water resist to patch my sand team's biggest holes.

Three targeted upgrades: Hydrapple replaces Chandelure with a Water/Ground-resistant Regenerator pivot (Giga Drain 4x SE on Swampert-Mega, Earth Power 2x SE on Metagross-Mega) — critical for the rain matchup while still hitting Steel types. Houndoom replaces the dead-weight Absol at equal cost with Dark/Fire typing, Flash Fire immunity, and Flamethrower/Heat Wave coverage (2x SE on Klefki). Rotom replaces Sandaconda with Levitate Ground immunity — the team's biggest structural hole — while adding Electric STAB (4x SE on Pelipper) and Ghost typing for the spam core.

I would consolidate the three weakest budget picks (Absol 1, Sandaconda 2, Chandelure 6 = 9 points) into one better Pokémon at the draft rather than waiting for the trade window to fix them — a 9-point Water resist like Gyarados or Milotic would have addressed the rain hole from day one.
